messages.author: 21900f2d8179b8b5
messages.subject: likelihood estimation
parts:
I have a question regarding likelihood estimation:

As part of a simulation study I need to calculate the likelihood of the
parameters of a half-normal key function combined with one or several cos=

ine
expansions (I cannot use Distance for this purpose because I need to

integrate the estimation of the ESW into the code running the simulation)=
. I
have no difficulties in measuring the likelihood for the half-normal part=

of
the detection function; but I am unaware about how I could incorporate a
cosine expansion into this. So my question is: how do I determine the
probability (i.e. density function) of an observation at a given distance=

,
given a half-normal key function (with its parameter) and one or several
cosine expansion terms (with their parameters)?

Thank you very much for your suggestion and help.

--

easier though to call the mcds estimation engine of Distance from your
code. An example of this is given at * |http://hdl.handle.net/10023/629|*

Steve Buckland
